ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Satchel Paige Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care for two years of breathlessness on exertion and a morning cough: history, examination, blood tests including alpha-1 antitrypsin and eosinophils, ECG, NT-proBNP, cardiovascular risk, vaccines, a reliever inhaler and a pulmonology consultation. Concerns: Breathless on stairs and on walks he used to take easily; He wants straight answers and his own numbers, and to be treated the same as anyone else; He wants to keep fishing and speaking to young people. [S]

tr.td: 12-lead ECG: sinus rhythm at 82; normal axis; no Q waves, ST changes or signs of right ventricular strain; P waves normal

Spirometry before and after 400 micrograms of albuterol, meeting ATS/ERS acceptability and repeatability standards, interpreted with the GLI Global race-neutral reference equations: post-bronchodilator FEV1 2.02 L (61% predicted), FVC 3.48 L, FEV1/FVC 0.58; a 0.10 L (5%) bronchodilator response

Low-dose CT of the chest for lung cancer screening: centrilobular emphysema, worst in the upper lobes; a 4 mm solid nodule in the right lower lobe (Lung-RADS 2, benign appearance); moderate coronary artery calcification; no mass or enlarged nodes
Outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation, twice a week for ten weeks (20 sessions): endurance and strength training, breathing techniques and education
Chest X-ray, posteroanterior and lateral: hyperinflated lungs with flattened diaphragms; no consolidation, effusion, pneumothorax or enlarged heart
Advance care planning conversation, about 25 minutes, with his consent
Ultrasound of the abdominal aorta for aneurysm screening: maximum diameter 2.4 cm; no aneurysm
12-lead ECG after the exacerbation: sinus rhythm at 76; unchanged from intake; no ischemic changes, arrhythmia or right heart strain

tr.td: Establishing primary care for two years of breathlessness on exertion and a morning cough: history, examination, blood tests including alpha-1 antitrypsin and eosinophils, ECG, NT-proBNP, cardiovascular risk, vaccines, a reliever inhaler and a pulmonology consultation

Two-week review on the day of the pulmonology consultation: spirometry with race-neutral interpretation, blood gas, six-minute walk, GOLD group and first maintenance inhaler, inhaler technique, pulmonary rehabilitation and lung cancer screening
Eight-week review: symptoms on the new inhaler, technique, rehabilitation, the screening CT and the lipid response
Fifteen-week review after an exacerbation and pulmonary rehabilitation: symptoms, exacerbation history, GOLD group, oxygen, the action plan and the plan ahead
Same-day sick visit for a COPD exacerbation

Breathlessness work-up at intake: symptoms with the CAT and mMRC, exacerbation history over the past year, smoking history and examination; blood count with eosinophils, alpha-1 antitrypsin once, kidney function, HbA1c, lipids, NT-proBNP and a 12-lead ECG; resting oxygen saturation read with care in darker skin
Pulmonology consultation to confirm the diagnosis with spirometry, interpret it with race-neutral equations, and advise on treatment, oxygen and rehabilitation
Albuterol with a spacer as needed for breathlessness, with technique checked at the visit

Maintenance therapy for GOLD group B: a LAMA with a LABA (umeclidinium with vilanterol) once daily; no inhaled corticosteroid with eosinophils below 0.10 x 10^3/uL and no exacerbations; inhaler technique and inspiratory effort checked at every visit; treatment reviewed at each follow-up for symptoms and exacerbations
Pulmonary rehabilitation: twice a week for about ten weeks, with six-minute walks at entry and exit, then a home exercise program

Oxygen: room-air arterial blood gas and six-minute walk oximetry; long-term oxygen only if resting PaO2 is 55 mm Hg or less (60 with cor pulmonale or polycythemia), confirmed twice; no long-term or ambulatory oxygen for moderate desaturation
Lung cancer screening: yearly low-dose CT at 50 to 80 with 20 or more pack-years, after shared decision-making, while he has quit within fifteen years and remains fit for treatment
Cardiovascular risk: moderate-intensity atorvastatin by shared decision, with a lipid panel at about eight weeks; blood pressure at each visit; ECG reviewed after any exacerbation
Vaccines: PCV20 and Tdap now; influenza, RSV and COVID-19 in the autumn; recombinant zoster
COPD action plan, spoken and written: what to do on a good day, when symptoms worsen (reliever, call the clinic the same day), and when to call 911; staying smoke-free
Find the cause of the breathlessness
COPD confirmed by spirometry (post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.58); heart failure unlikely (NT-proBNP 92, normal ECG); alpha-1 antitrypsin normal
Six-minute walk 360 to 425 m after rehabilitation; CAT 18 to 11
Fewer and milder flare-ups, treated early
One moderate exacerbation treated at home within a day of starting, using the action plan; no hospital stay
LDL 148 to 86 mg/dL on atorvastatin 20 mg
PCV20 and Tdap at intake; influenza, RSV, COVID-19 and the first zoster dose at the wellness visit
